```{r,fig.showtext=TRUE}
multiplesheets <- function(fname) { 
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(fname) 
  tibble <- lapply(sheets, function(x) readxl::read_excel(fname, sheet = x, skip = 1)) 
  data_frame <- lapply(tibble, as.data.frame) 
  names(data_frame) <- sheets 
  #print(data_frame) 
} 

pagebreak <- function() {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
        return("\\newpage")
  }
  else {
        return('<div style="page-break-before: always;" />')
  }
} # end of functions
```

This report was automatically generated using the TEA-CART tool.

## 1.Introduction

The Transportation Evaluation and Carbon Reduction Tool (TEA-CART) is a comprehensive and dynamic tool aimed at assisting states with selecting and prioritizing transportation capital program investments to effectively support greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction. The tool is designed to accept inputs typically available during the programming process. It provides key outputs including:

-   A baseline inventory and forecast of GHG emissions.

-   GHG impacts of a capital program or a hypothetical set of capital projects.

-   Information on cost-effectiveness of various project types.

TEA-CART is a planning-level tool. It is designed to accept relatively simple inputs, typically available at the long-range planning or programming stage, characterizing the number, size, context, and type of transportation projects that could reduce GHG emissions. As such, TEA-CART relies on data that is typical for projects of a given type. In practice, individual projects may results in a wide range of GHG effects. For more detailed, project-specific evaluation, users may want to refer to project-specific tools such as the Federal Highway Administration Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Program (CMAQ) Emissions Calculator Toolkit.

### 2.1 Baseline GHG Forecast

#### 2.1.1 Transportation GHG Forecast

```{r, results="asis",fig.align = 'left', fig.showtext=TRUE}

# load dummy data
# path2 <- paste0(getwd(),'/data/dummy_output.xlsx')

ghg_dat <- params$ghg_data
# ghg_dat[nrow(ghg_dat), "Total (All Transportation)"] <- "Change from Base Year (%)"

# str(ghg_dat)
GHG_forecast <- ghg_dat %>%
  slice(1:(n() - 1)) %>% # get rid of thte last row 
    pivot_longer(cols = !(`Emissions`), names_to = c("year"), values_to = 'Emission')
# 
# GHG_forecast <- readxl::read_excel(path2, sheet = 'GHG Forecast') %>%
#     pivot_longer(cols = !(`Emissions (MT CO2e)`), names_to = c("year"), values_to = 'Emission')

fig_list <- c("Total (Onroad Vehicles)", "Total (All Transportation)")

for ( var in fig_list){
  
    if (var == 'Total (Onroad Vehicles)') {
    title <- "On-Road Transportation Emissions"
  } else if (var == 'Total (All Transportation)') {
    title <- "All Transportation Emissions"
  }
  
  data_temp <- GHG_forecast %>%
    filter(`Emissions` == var)
  
  ghg_fore <- ggplot(data_temp,
               aes(y = Emission, x = year, group = 1)) +
    geom_line(color = '#E69F00', size = 1) + 
    geom_point(color = '#E69F00', size = 3) + 
    ylab("Emissions (MT CO2e) ") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)) + 
    xlab(NULL) +
    ggtitle(title) +
        theme_classic() 
# print(ghg_fore +  theme_classic())
  print(ghg_fore + theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12)
  ))

  
  print(tagList(cat("  \n\n  ")))
      print(tagList(cat("  \\newpage  ")))
      print(tagList(cat("  \n\n  ")))
}
```

```{r, results="asis",fig.align = 'left', fig.showtext=TRUE}
source_list <- c(head(unique(GHG_forecast$`Emissions`),6))
year_list <- c(unique(GHG_forecast$year))

# print(check)
for ( var in year_list){
  data_temp <- GHG_forecast %>%
    filter(`Emissions` %in% source_list, year == var) %>%
    mutate(fraction = Emission/sum(.$Emission),
           ymax =  cumsum(fraction),
           ymin = c(0, head(ymax, n=-1)),
           labelPosition = (ymax + ymin)/ 2,
           `Emission Source` = paste0(`Emissions` ," (",round(fraction *100,digits = 1), " %",")"))
  
print(ggplot(data_temp,
             aes(ymax = ymax,
                 ymin = ymin,
                 xmax = 4,
                 xmin = 3,
                 fill = `Emission Source`)) +
  geom_rect(color = NA) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'RdYlBu') +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(c(2, 4)) +
  ggtitle(paste0('Transportation Emission: ', var))+
   ggplot2::theme_void() +
   ggplot2::theme(
     plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
     plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
     legend.text.align = 0
   )
) + theme_classic() 
    
print(tagList(cat("  \n\n  ")))
      print(tagList(cat("  \\newpage  ")))
      print(tagList(cat("  \n\n  ")))
}
```

```{r, results="asis",fig.align = 'left', fig.showtext=TRUE}
indicators <- unique(scenarioresults$indicator)

  for (i in indicators){
data_temp <- scenarioresults %>%
  filter(indicator == i, !is.na(mt_reduction)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  mutate(Year = as.factor(Year)) %>%
  mutate(Scenario = ifelse(Scenario == 'Scenario1', 'Scenario 1', 'Scenario 2'))

  scen <- ggplot(data_temp,
               aes(fill = Scenario,
                   y = mt_reduction,
                   x = Year))+
    geom_bar(position="dodge", stat="identity")+
       scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)) +

      ggtitle(paste0("Reduction in ", i, " (From Baseline)")) +
            theme_classic() +
          xlab(NULL)

print(scen + theme(

))
```
